agent_answer.notes: The corpus (5 papers: S001, S002, S003, S004, S005) gives a mixed answer to whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves the factual accuracy of LLM-generated answers. Three papers (S001, S002, S005) find RAG improves factual accuracy / reduces hallucination; one (S004) finds no measurable improvement; and one (S003) finds RAG increases hallucinated content. Each study used a single 1,000-question benchmark (BioClaimQA, LawFactQA, MedAnswerSet, TriviaCheck, SciFactBench respectively), a single generator and a single run, so results are domain- and setting-specific and not directly pooled. Overall, across the corpus, RAG does not uniformly improve factual accuracy: it helps in some domains (S001, S002, S005), is neutral in one (S004), and hurts in medical QA (S003). All per-paper numbers and benchmark names are quoted directly from the corpus files and recorded as accepted claims (claim-000001 through claim-000015).

retrieval augmentation makes the generated answers clearly more accurate (766/1000 (76.6%) factually correct from parameters vs 91.5% with document-index retrieval, on SciFactBench)
